[107936535][TR] [Online Purchasing]Medallia Alert
Generated: 2026-09-21T13:11:00.000Z

Issue:
Customer reported difficulty completing an online purchase on the Samsung Turkey eStore, requiring three separate attempts before the order went through. The customer was using a mobile Android device with Chrome (version 151.0.7922.202) and attempting to pay with a credit or debit card. Order TR260916-85147821 was eventually placed successfully.

RCA:
Backend logs were checked in SAP Cloud Logging (Kibana MENA) for order TR260916-85147821 across the Sep 16-17 timeframe and also without time restriction. No ERROR-level logs were found for this order code across any index. The order is currently in SHIPPED status and has progressed through the full order lifecycle without any platform errors.

The logs contain 4,440 entries for this order code, all dated Sep 21, 2026, with only WARN-level entries from TokoFraudServicesClientImpl ("Have no line items so ignore this order") and TokoSMSServiceImpl ("SMS page not found"). These are standard post-fulfilment warnings and do not indicate any checkout or payment failure.

The payment mode used is tr-masterpassPaymentMode (MasterPass, the Turkish payment provider). The customer mentioned paying with credit or debit card, which maps to the MasterPass flow on the TR storefront. The order confirmation URL contains viewEnd=true, confirming the order was successfully completed.

The fact that the customer required three attempts to complete the purchase suggests intermittent friction during the checkout or payment submission flow, likely on the frontend or payment gateway side. The absence of any backend ERROR logs means the Hybris platform processed all three attempts without throwing exceptions. The first two attempts would have resulted in TEMPORARY or TEMPORARY_CANCEL orders that were cleaned up by the standard temporary order cleanup workflow, while the third attempt succeeded.

This is expected behaviour. The Hybris platform handled all checkout attempts correctly. No payment-related errors, session expiry errors, or cart invalidation errors were found in the backend logs for this order.

Possible remediation:
No platform remediation is required. The order TR260916-85147821 was successfully placed and is in SHIPPED status. The checkout friction experienced by the customer appears to be a frontend or payment gateway interaction issue (possibly card validation, 3D Secure redirect, or MasterPass authentication), not a Hybris platform defect. If the issue recurs frequently for TR region customers, investigation should focus on the MasterPass payment gateway integration and 3D Secure authentication flow for potential timeouts or UX improvements.

Regards

Aryan

Generated: 2026-09-21

Hi [~arjenelle.a@samsung.com] ,

Order SA260730-45663184 was placed on Jul 31 with Checkout.com (checkoutDotComFlowPaymentMode) for 31.00 SAR. The payment AUTHORIZATION and CAPTURE both completed successfully on the same day. However, the order process (order-process-v25-69) failed early in the fulfilment flow shortly after consignment creation, with endMessage "Order failed". The consignment process (consignment-process-v11-36) also failed with endMessage "Order not placed."

The refund step in the order process is the action "refundCancelOrder" (bean refundCancelOrderActionV3), which sits in the cancellation path: waitForCancelledOrder -> isChargeBackRefundProcessed -> isInstantRefundEnabledCheckBeforeFinancialUpdate -> refundCancelOrder -> sendRefundNotification -> failed. This path is only reachable while the order process is still active and progressing through its defined states.

Because the order process entered the "failed" end state immediately after the consignment failure, it never reached the cancellation/refund branch. The process treats "failed" as a terminal state. The order was subsequently set to CANCELLED on Aug 6 (via external/backoffice action), but this status change does not re-engage the business process. The sendOrderCancelledEmailProcess ran separately and successfully, but the payment refund, which is part of the order-process-v25-69 flow, was never triggered.

The DB was checked on Sep 21 and confirms only two PaymentTransactionEntry records exist: AUTHORIZATION-1 (ACCEPTED, 31.00 SAR) and CAPTURE-2 (ACCEPTED, 31.00 SAR). No REFUND entry was ever created.

Regarding the duplicate refund concern: the order process is in FAILED state (terminal), the order status is CANCELLED, and no automated mechanism will trigger a refund on this order going forward. The manual refund from PG is the only refund that has occurred. Auto refund will not happen on this order.

The order process was manually moved to failed state on Sep 17 to stop the 48-day loop between WaitForWarehouse and WaitForSendToWarehouse. The consignment is in CANCELLED status since Sep 17.

Thanks,
Aryan.

Ticket Summary: Update or create Cronjob for autocleanup
Generated: 2026-09-03T20:00:00Z

Hi Arvind ,

The SMI cluster database is experiencing recurring high storage issues because several Hybris snapshot tables and custom event log tables grow unboundedly without any automated retention cleanup. SAP has raised incident 002075129500011086542026 and advised running batched DELETE statements from HAC per KBA 3716653, but this is a manual workaround and needs to be automated as a scheduled cronjob.

The six target tables fall into two categories. First, snapshot tables generated by Hybris when snapshot persistence is enabled for standard types: users4sn (User, typecode 4), paymentinfos42sn (PaymentInfo, typecode 42), pricerows1055sn (PriceRow, typecode 1055), and addresses23sn (Address, typecode 23). These tables follow Hybris naming convention where the numeric suffix is the typecode and the sn suffix denotes snapshot. They accumulate every versioned snapshot for their respective types and have no built-in expiry mechanism. Second, the tasklogs table which is the standard Hybris process engine task log, accumulating process execution metadata. Third, the tokoeventlog table which is a custom type defined in tokocore-items.xml at line 38446 with deployment table TokoEventLog and typecode 11164. The TokoEventLog type stores event messages with a target item reference, a message string, and an infoMap, indexed by itemtype, target, and creationtime. Both tasklogs and tokoeventlog are write-heavy tables that grow continuously during normal operation.

No existing DB-level cleanup cronjob exists in the Toko codebase for these tables. The codebase has several domain-specific cleanup jobs (CachedServiceabilityCleanupJob, TokoOtpSessionCleanupJob, TokoSimContractDocumentCleanupJob, TokoBackofficeReportsCleanupJobPerformable, TokoTradeInDataCleanupJob, AltchaCleanupJob), but all operate through the Hybris model layer using FlexibleSearch and ModelService.remove, not through raw SQL DELETE statements. The SAP-requested queries use DELETE TOP(200000) with DATEADD-based retention filtering, which is a SQL Server batched-delete pattern that bypasses the model layer entirely. This is intentional for performance: deleting 200K rows at a time avoids lock escalation and transaction log bloat on large tables.

A PC ticket PC-53529 has already been created for this work, titled "[SAM-24720] Create DB cleanup cronjobs for SMI cluster" and is currently in To Do status. A previous similar ticket SAM-20914 ("Update or create Cronjob for autocleanup") was resolved as Closed, and HGE-8069 ("TokoEventLog Cleanup") is in Launch Verification status, indicating prior work has been done on TokoEventLog cleanup specifically. The ticket SAM-18467 ("Please check tasklog, tokoeventlog table size") was also completed, confirming these table sizes have been monitored before.

The recommended approach is to create a new JobPerformable class, TokoDbCleanupJobPerformable, in the tokocore extension that executes the six batched DELETE statements using direct JDBC (not FlexibleSearch) to match the SQL Server-specific syntax. The job should be configurable via project.properties for retention periods and batch sizes, scheduled via a CronJob instance with a Trigger in tokodeployment ImpEx, and configured to run during low-traffic windows. The existing PC-53529 should cover this implementation. The job should be created on all SMI cluster environments where snapshot persistence is enabled. No Kibana log analysis or HAC FlexiQuery was performed for this ticket as it is a database maintenance request, not an order-level issue.

Thanks,

Aryan

## Remediation

1. PC-53529 already exists for this work. Implement the TokoDbCleanupJobPerformable in tokocore with the six DELETE statements as specified.
2. Configure retention periods via project.properties: toko.db.cleanup.tasklogs.retention.months=2, toko.db.cleanup.users.retention.months=1, toko.db.cleanup.paymentinfo.retention.months=3, toko.db.cleanup.pricerows.retention.months=3, toko.db.cleanup.addresses.retention.months=3, toko.db.cleanup.tokoeventlog.retention.months=3
3. Create CronJob instance and Trigger via ImpEx in tokodeployment, scheduled to run daily during off-peak hours.
4. Deploy to SMI cluster environments. Verify table sizes decrease after first run.
5. Refer to HGE-8069 for prior TokoEventLog cleanup work and SAM-20914 for the previous autocleanup implementation pattern.
